text: {"kind":"final","content":"{\"answer\":\"The data: overall on-time rate 71.0% vs the 94.0% benchmark; 48,340 deliveries and 14,019 late; penalties of $872,460 and handling cost of $476,646; 9 at-risk accounts representing $14,200,000 revenue; 67.3% of late deliveries have a cause before pickup (incomplete address, order after cut-off, non-nearest warehouse, carrier lane, route detour).\\n\\nWhat routing can fix: booking better carriers and blocking lanes plus fixing route overruns (“Carrier lanes + routes”) would raise on-time to 80.4%, avoiding late avoided 4,523 and cost avoided $409,897 in costs. Fixing causes before pickup (“Address + cut-off + stock”) would raise on-time to 87.8%, avoiding late avoided 8,112 and cost avoided $801,412 in costs.\\n\\nEvidence summary: routing improvements alone lift on-time from 71.0% to 80.4% (late avoided 4,523; cost avoided $409,897). Addressing pre-pickup causes raises on-time further to 87.8% (late avoided 8,112; cost avoided $801,412). The highest on-time in the replay is when pre-pickup causes plus lane rules are fixed together (96.3%).\\n\\nSuggestion (from the data, not a decision): the data points to greater gains from fixing pre-pickup causes than from routing alone (87.8% vs 80.4% on-time; late avoided 8,112 vs 4,523). What would change this is larger avoided late deliveries or cost savings from the routing-only row than the values shown. The decision stays with Halcyon.\",\"refused\":false}"}
